Title: Combined discussion on Statutory Resolution regarding Disapproval of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (No. 8 of 2021) and Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Bill, 2021(Statutory Resolution-Negatived and Government Bill-Passed). 

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Now, the House will take up Item No. 18 and 19 together.

SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB (CUTTACK): Sir, I beg to move:

“That this House disapproves of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (8 of 2021) promulgated by the President on 30 September, 2021”

THE MINISTER OF FINANCE AND MINISTER OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS (SHRIMATI NIRMALA SITHARAMAN): Sir, I beg to move:

“That the Bill further to amend the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, 1985, be taken into consideration.”

Sir, actually, on this Amendment Bill, which we are bringing now -- and I am sure that the hon. Member Mahatab, while he would rise to have his objections mentioned -- I would be keen to put my arguments before on the assumptions that he objects on certain grounds; and in this case, for presuming his statement, I feel that there is no ground on which this particular Amendment Bill can be objected. It is because the primary reason for any party being in the Opposition, even if we were to be there, to object an Ordinance is: ‘you do not legislate through Ordinances; you need to have a proper legislation going through the House.’ 

Whereas in this case, that is exactly what we are trying to do. We are trying to bring in a legislation where an Ordinance had to come, and the reasons for the Ordinance to have to come between the Sessions is well explained, and I am quite willing to state the explanations before the hon. Members.

Sir, so, an Ordinance came in for certain reasons which I shall explain. Today, we are coming in to say that the Ordinance be replaced by a Bill. That, I think, is an ideal situation because we are bringing in a Bill so that the House can legislate and take it up for consideration.

Now, the Ordinance was necessitated because of a court order. First of all, the content of the Bill and the content of the Ordinance are all absolutely as was decided by the court and as should have been done even otherwise. It was as a result of a little clerical error, an error in which some of the cross-referencing Sections were not corrected when an Amendment was being brought in sometime in 2014.

Therefore, the Bombay High Court Bench in Goa noticed it and said: “Yes, there is this anomaly but that can be understood from the intent of the legislation and allowed it to remain.” ‘Remain’ means, they did not say for retaining it but they kept it and said: “Go ahead with the Act because where it should be overlooked, you can.” I am only paraphrasing the words of the Court. Subsequently, in the Tripura High Court, the same matter came up and the Court felt whilst the Bombay High Court, Goa Bench understood it but they did not agree and said that correction will have to be affected immediately keeping in line with the intent of the Court. It is that correction of that anomaly which the Bombay High Court’s Goa Bench saw and kept the spirit of the Act intact. Similarly, here, the Tripura High Court noticed it but wanted an immediate correction. It is because they wanted an immediate correction, the Ordinance had to be brought in only to the limited extent of correcting the anomaly and it is that and nothing more than the Ordinance. There is not one more criminality or anything else being brought in the Bill which is now coming. It is exactly the same as the Ordinance which is getting replaced here. So, with this said, I would think, hon. learned Member Bhartruhari ji will agree and hope he does not find a reason to have to get up and voice his opposition to it. 

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Motions moved:

“That this House disapproves of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (8 of 2021) promulgated by the President on 30 September, 2021”

“That the Bill further to amend the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances, 1985, be taken into consideration.”

SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB: Sir, repeatedly, I have been opposing law making position of the Government and last time on a different Ordinance I had specifically mentioned that how many Ordinances per year have been moved by the present Government. During the UPA regime, I had also mentioned how many Ordinances have been moved by the UPA regime. Before that, the first NDA Government also had moved a number of Ordinances and the average was, actually, increasing year after year. This provision of Ordinance is a very unique feature in our Constitution and, especially, in our sub-continent, this is a unique feature which we have inherited from the British Parliament. But Britain does not have this provision of Ordinance any more. It is high time that we should also do away with the Ordinance mechanism. Yes, we sit in four Sessions – Budget Session in two parts, Winter Session and Monsoon Session – whereas the British Parliament sits invariably throughout the year. There are a large number of Parliaments in the world which sit throughout the year. Here, it is because we have Sessions and Inter-Sessions in between, sometimes, law-making has to be done through Ordinance. That is the logic which repeatedly a number of Governments have given. But I still hold the view that it is not correct to make a law through Ordinance and then subsequently when the Session is called, withdraw the Ordinance and place the Bill for consideration. There are instances. I would not go into that aspect when and how the Ordinance had to be withdrawn or had become nullified because the House did not agree. Here, I would like to mention that this Bill, specifically the Bill that is now under consideration, suffers from incongruities and is also illegal. The hon. Minister just now mentioned about the Bombay High Court Goa Bench and also subsequently about the Tripura High Court. When will the House be enlightened? When will we become aware? When did the Tripura High Court pronounce that Judgement? What is the duration when the Ordinance came into being? That will clear a lot of confusion that is there in this country. 

I would come directly to the provision, the Fundamental Rights, that I had mentioned the other day which is related to Article 21.

It says:

“No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of the law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence, nor be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence” … Interruptions 

I am talking about Article 20 (1) which talks about protection in respect of conviction for offences. In this respect, I would say, there is a wide acceptance that amendments to the Taxation Laws may apply retrospectively where the Government has announced by Press release. During the UPA Regime, we have seen that an amendment was done to impose tax retrospectively. At that time, the then Political Party which was in Opposition, both in Rajya Sabha and also in Lok Sabha, had said vehemently that they oppose that. Subsequently, in 2014, when the Party came to power, they also effected this change. But here, I would just like to mention that retrospective effect is not allowed in criminal law. The protection given in the Constitution has been the main source of all other judgments with respect to penal provisions in tax cases. The judgment has made it well settled that there cannot be any retrospectivity in respect of penalty and confiscation. In the Statement of Objects and Reasons, the word ‘inadvertently’ is mentioned. The consequential changes were not carried out in Section 27 (A) of the NDPS Act at the time of amendment in Section 2 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Act, 2014. But how is it possible? This leads to another question that this House had deliberated in 2011. In March, 2011, the then Finance Minister, Mr. Pranab Mukherjee had moved that amendment. Subsequently, in 2011, perhaps within six months’ time, the Standing Committee on Finance had given the Report. I can share it because now, it is in public domain. Subsequently, a question was asked:

“The necessity of the amendment that you are moving in 2011 came to light in 2001 law. Why it took more than 10 years to move the amendment?”

The answer to this question that the Department had given at that time was too frivolous. I have that Report with me. It said: 

“The Government changed, and a number of procedures had to be followed.”

But it took 10 years to make that amendment. Now, what is happening is this. This is the Act which came into force in 2014. We came to know about what is called as clerical error after the Goa Bench of Bombay High Court’s attention was drawn. Subsequently, the Tripura High Court said that they have to correct it. I will come to what the Tripura High Court has actually pronounced. But this shows, if I may say so, the lackadaisical approach of the Ministry or the Department, invariably whoever is there in the Government, be it UPA or the NDA, that how they have functioned, especially relating to this important law. What does the law say? The basic change that was effected is this. It says that those who deal with narcotics, who harbour offenders, should be punished. 

15.00hrs

Those, who indulge in financing illicit traffickings, should be punished. This was the intent. If this is the intent, how come a mistake has been committed and this mistake is to be corrected after seven years? This is a mistake that was to be incorporated over 10 years from 2001 to 2011 and when it was notified in 2014, it takes another seven years. In 2021, you are making this effort. I may be wrong. I hope I am wrong. I believe again to have a retrospective effect, which actually leads to double jeopardy, which is illegal, you are taking this after-effect with your majority and getting it passed in the Rajya Sabha. If at all it becomes an Act, again it will be decided in the court of law.

But here I would like to apprise this House. On three occasions, of course, retrospective effect has taken place. The essentiality of a right to protection from retrospective criminal law has generally been accepted without argument. Literature on the justification for the principle is very scarce. Yet, it has become well-accepted that individuals have such a right. The principle has been enunciated in various declarations of human rights from 1789 until the present. Nevertheless, there are some examples. I would refer to only three. I am mentioning here three examples of retrospective law-making. One is Nuremberg trials of the late 1940s. The second is the decision of the House of Lords in Shaw vs. Director of Public Prosecutions in 1961 and the third is, the Commonwealth’s ‘bottom of the harbour’ tax legislation of 1982. These are the three instances which history tells us, yes, retrospective penal provision can be effected, but these are totally different from the provision that we are accepting here.

Here, I would like to mention that in each case the actions of the defendants were considered so morally repugnant that the principle of non-retroactivity was relaxed so as to allow them to be punished. These examples differ to the extent to which the retrospective aspect of each has been accepted. The Nazi trials at Nuremberg are generally said to have been adjudged fairly. The decision in Shaw’s case has been criticized widely, and the ‘bottom of the harbour’ tax legislation has attracted both critics and champions. 

Retrospective operation is an inaccurate term and open to various interpretations. I would say the word, ‘retrospective’ is somewhat very ambiguous. Ordinarily, a canon of interpretation of penal legislation does not permit the penal provisions to have retrospective effect. But Article 20, sub-section (1) does not bar a civil liability being imposed retrospectively. What is prohibited under Article 20(1) is only conviction or sentence but not trial.

A person can be convicted and punished under a law in force which means a law factually in existence at the time the offence was committed. A law passed on 30th September but an act committed on 1st August, cannot be taken to be a law in force on 1st August, and so an act committed on 1st August cannot be punished thereunder. A law, not factually in existence at the time, enacted subsequently but by a legislative declaration deemed to have become operative from an earlier date, cannot be considered to be a law factually in force earlier than the date of its enactment. But what I understand from the hon. Minister’s version is that it was in law in a part but it was absent in the penalty clause. A question was posed and this question also is of greater importance. Is financing illicit trafficking of narcotics and harbouring offenders no longer a crime in India? To address that question, these amendments have been made. What does the provision that was omitted in the Act read? The provision reads:

“Whoever indulges in financing, directly or indirectly, any, of the activities specified in sub-clauses (i) to (v) of clause (viiia) of section 2 or harbours any person engaged in any of the aforementioned activities, shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to twenty years and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to two lakh rupees:

Provided that the court may, for reasons to be recorded in the judgment, impose a fine exceeding two lakh rupees.”

The Act which has evolved over the years and has been amended thrice earlier, and this is the fourth time, is before us. In the Ordinance, it was mentioned ‘due to oversight’. It was also said that there was a drafting error. Now, we hear that it is a clerical error. Omission is noticed after seven years, as I mentioned. What the relevant cause was, that I have also mentioned. So, why did the provision become inoperable? That is the question, 

I hope the hon. Minister will tell us. I have also read the text of the provisions. But Section 2, sub section (viiia), sub clause (i) to (v), which is supposed to be the catalogue of offences, does not exist after the 2014 amendment. If Section 27A penalises a blank list or a non-existent provision, it can be argued that it is virtually inoperable. 

In 2016, an accused sought bail citing this omission before a special judge in West Tripura in Agartala. The District Judge referred the case to the Tripura High Court. The Law Ministry had argued, and this is the beauty of the argument here, that the court must overlook the omission and read the legislation as a whole. It also told the court that the provision would be amended to rectify the dissonance. The Tripura High Court agreed with the Government’s view but said, “It may not be the best solution”. 

Now, I come to the second aspect that is recent judgement of hon. Tripura High Court which prompted the Government to take remedial steps to correct the anomaly. The case no. is Cr1.Ref.1/2020 Court On Its Own Motion vs. Union of India. 

The Court came to your rescue and asked to take appropriate steps for amendment as required in Section 27A. I have my doubt whether this insertion by the Court is appropriate. Therefore, I hold the view that criminal laws cannot be amended retrospectively. 

Article 20 of the Constitution guarantees protection against double jeopardy. Article 20(1) says, 

“No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence, nor be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence…”

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Mahtab ji, please conclude. 

SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB: If this is the case, how can the penal provision be enforced retrospectively. ....(Interruptions) 

As I had said, it will lead to more constitutional questions. 

My question here is: When we accept it was a mistake, why should we commit another mistake by making it retrospective? We are all for the change, by adding this provision in Section 27A, but by making it retrospective, we will make another mistake. There is a flaw in the law. You correct the flaw. It is necessary. We are all for it. I am for it, but by making it retrospective, you are making another mistake which will also be challenged in the court of law and we will wait. 

I have no idea what effect this will have against the alleged culprits who have been apprehended for a large haul of narcotic drugs from a Gujarat port. I believe, appropriate steps are being taken. We need a strong law, a law that is implementable, clear and swift. Thank you.

डॉ. सुभाष रामराव भामरे (धुले) : सभापति महोदय, धन्यवाद । मैं आपका आभारी हूं, क्योंकि आपने मुझे इस महत्वपूर्ण बिल पर अपनी बात रखने का अवसर दिया है । मैं द नार्कोटिक ड्रग्स एण्ड साइकोट्रोपिक सब्स्टैन्सेस (अमेंडमेंट) बिल, 2021 के समर्थन में खड़ा हुआ हूं । 

This Bill seeks to replace the Ordinance which was promulgated on 30th September, 2021. The Government has put into effect the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021, amending Section 27A of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985. This has been done to correct a drafting error. 

As you know, Sir, the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act came into force on 14th November, 1985 and is the principal legislation through which the State regulates certain operations such as manufacture, transport and consumption that is related to narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. The Act has evolved over years and it has been amended thrice – in 1988, in 2001 and in 2014 – which has changed its scope and direction. The prevention of illicit trafficking in the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act was passed in 1988 and brought in to ensure full implementation and enforcement of the Act. 

Now, I come to what the need for the Ordinance was. The Ordinance is intended to rectify a drafting error. In 2014, the Act was amended and the section relating to the definition of such illicit activity was changed. However, the section on penalty for financing these illicit activities was not amended and continued to refer to the earlier definition. The Ordinance amends the section on penalty to change the reference to the new section. 

This amendment will be deemed to have been in effect from 1st May, 2014, that is, when the 2014 amendment came into effect. Whoever indulges in financing, directly or indirectly, any of the activities specified in sub-clauses (1) to (5) of clause 8A of Section 2 or harbours any person engaged in any of the aforementioned activities shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than 10 years, but which can be extended to 20 years, and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may be expanded to two lakh rupees.

However, sub-clauses of clause (viiia) of section 2 of the NDPS Act was amended, relettered and relocated at clause (viiib) of section of the NDPS Act by the NDPS (Amendment) Act, 2014, which came into effect from 1st March, 2014. Also, clause (viii) of section 2 was relettered, which says: ‘essential narcotic drug’ means a narcotic drug notified by the Central Government for medical and scientific use. But the corresponding amendment was not made in section 27A.

The Tripura High Court in a significant verdict discovered that an oversight in drafting the 2014 amendment to the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act of 1985 had unintentionally rendered the key provision of section 27A which provides for the punishment of those financing illicit trafficking inoperable. The Tripura High Court noticed this anomaly and directed the Central Government to take appropriate steps for amending section 27A after an accused sought bail before a special judge in West Tripura in Agartala citing this omission in drafting.

In 2016, an accused was sought before a special judge in West Tripura in Agartala citing this omission in drafting. The accused plea was that since section 27A penalised a blank list, he could not be charged under the offence. The District Judge then referred this case to the Tripura High Court. In the Hight Court, Law Ministry had argued that the court must overlook the omission and read the legislation as a whole. It also told the court that the provision would be amended to rectify the dissonance. The Tripura High Court agreed with the Government’s view but said that it may not be the best solution. The High Court directed to take appropriate steps for amendment as required in section 27A. Hence, with a view to having a correct interpretation and implementation of the NDPS Act, it was decided to rectify the anomaly in section 27A of the Act by substituting clause (viiib) of section 2 in place of clause (viiia) of section 2.

As the Parliament was not in Session and urgent legislation was required to be made, the President promulgated the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 on 30th September, 2021 for rectifying the said anomaly by substituting in 27A of the NDPS Act the reference of clause (viiib) of section 2 for clause (viiia) of section 2. The amendment does not create any new offence but contains a legislative declaration that reference of clause (viiia) always meant the corresponding renumbered provision in clause (viiib) and the amendment seeks to rectify this anomaly by making changes in section 27A of the said Act in order to carry out legislative intent of the statute, which has always been to read clause (viiib) in section 27A as already stood therein. This Bill seeks to replace the aforesaid Ordinance.

The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, which is commonly referred to as the NDPS Act, is an Act of the Parliament of India that prohibits a person the production, manufacturing, cultivation, possession, sale, purchasing, transport, storage, and/or consumption of any narcotic drug or psychotropic substance.

The Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on 23rd August, 1985. It was passed by both the Houses of Parliament. It came into force on 14 November, 1985. The NDPS Act has since been amended thrice – In 1988, 2001 and 2014. The Act extends to the whole of India and it applies to all Indian citizens outside India and to all persons on ships and aircraft registered in India.

The Narcotic Control Bureau (NCB) was set up under this Act with effect from March, 1986. हाल ही में एनसीबी लाइमलाइट में आया था । आपको मालूम होगा कि एक साल पहले या छ: महीने पहले there were cases of drug abuse in Bollywood. I would not name the people, but that has reflected how deeply this drug menace has entered into the society. हमने देखा कि उसमें बॉलीवुड के बहुत सारे सेलिब्रिटीज़ के नाम आए । अभी कुछ महीने पहले एक हिंदी सुपरस्टार का लड़का क्रूज़ में ड्रग्स के साथ पकड़ा गया, जिसके बाद इन्वेस्टिगेशन हुई । … (व्यवधान) 

डॉ. मोहम्मद जावेद (किशनगंज) : उसके पास कोई ड्रग्स नहीं मिला । … (व्यवधान) 

डॉ. सुभाष रामराव भामरे : वह बात अलग है, लेकिन बहुत सारे बॉलिवुड सेलिब्रिट्रीज़ के नाम सामने आए । … (व्यवधान) मेरा कहने का मतलब ड्रग-मेनेस के बारे में है । … (व्यवधान) उसके पास ड्रग मिला या नहीं मिला, लेकिन बहुत सारे सेलिब्रिटीज़ के नाम लिए गए । … (व्यवधान)… I am an Oncologist surgeon, मैं जानता हूं ।

SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SADANAND SULE (BARAMATI): Sir, to talk about somebody’s child like this . … (Interruptions)

SHRI KALYAN BANERJEE (SREERAMPUR): The matter is sub judice in the court. 

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Hon. Member, you are aware that this matter is sub judice and it is under consideration by the court. Kindly avoid such remarks. 

DR. SUBHASH RAMRAO BHAMRE: My intention is simple. स्ट्रिंजेंट-लॉज़ के साथ लॉ-इनफोर्सिंग एजेंसीज़ काम कर रही है, लेकिन फिर भी बहुत सारे केसेज़ सामने आए हैं । … (Interruptions). The Narcotic Control Bureau (NCB) was set up under this Act with effect from March, 1986. 

This Act is designed to fulfil India’s treaty obligations under the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, Convention on Psychotropic Substances, and United Nations Convention against Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances. 

This Act was brought to Parliament to consolidate and amend the law relating to narcotic drugs, to make stringent provisions for the control and regulation of operations relating to narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, to provide for the forfeiture of property derived from, or used in illicit traffic in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. 

India had no legislation regarding narcotics until 1985. Cannabis smoking in India has been known since at least 2000 BC and it is first mentioned in the Atharvaveda, which dates back a few hundred years BC. The Indian Hemp Drugs Commission - cannabis is also known as hemp - an Indo-British study of cannabis usage in India was appointed in 1893. 

It found that the moderate use of hemp drugs was practically attended by no evil results at all and produces no injurious effects on the mind and no moral injury whatever. But regarding excessive use of the drug, the Commission concluded that it may certainly be accepted as very injurious. Cannabis and its derivatives marijuana, hashish, charas and bhang were legally sold in India until 1985. Their recreational use was at common places. Consumption of cannabis was not viewed as being similar to consumption of alcohol.

महोदय, मैं इसके बारे में यह बताना चाहता हूं कि इस एक्ट से पहले हमारे देश में क्या परिस्थिति थी । I am an Onco-Surgeon. When I was a medical student in 1974, तब हमारे कैम्पस के बाहर कैनबिस की जितनी भी वैराइटीज हैं, वे आसानी से अवेलेबल होती थीं and a good number of students fell prey to drug abuse. Hence, this Act was necessary, and I congratulate the Government for the same.

Consumption of cannabis was not seen as a socially deviant behaviour and was viewed as being similar to consumption of alcohol. Ganja and charas were considered by the upper-class Indians as poor man’s intoxicant although the rich consumed bhang during Holi. 

The United States began to campaign for a world-wide law against the drug क्योंकि यूनाइटेड स्टेट्स में पूरी युवा पीढ़ी इसकी गिरफ्त में आ रही थी । Hence, United States began to campaign for a world-wide law against the drug following the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs in 1961. However, India opposed the move and withstood American pressure to make cannabis illegal for nearly 25 years. American pressure increased in 1980, and in 1985, the then Government succumbed and enacted NDPS Act banning all narcotic drugs in India. 

India has a long history of opium and cannabis use, especially for medicines. I am a Onco-Surgeon and I can tell you that there are many types of cancers and only a few types of cancer are curable. In the remaining types of cancer, we prolong disease-free life. लेकिन जब रेक्रेंस होता है और स्टेज-4 का कैंसर होता है, तो there is excruciating pain and पेन होने की वजह से वे एक मिनट के लिए भी सो नहीं पाते हैं । ऐसे पेसेंट के लिए मॉरफिन बहुत जरूरी होती है । मॉरफिन की वजह से पेशेंट 6-7 घंटे तक सो पाते हैं । Hence, these drugs are equally important for medicines. 

Law enforcing agencies are of the view that a number of chemicals in the Schedule List should be increased as traffickers find ways to circumvent the existing rules by importing and exporting chemicals outside the List and then use it to manufacture psychotropic substances.

According to the Department of Revenue possession up to 1 kg. is termed as small quantity of cannabis and for commercial quantity, it is involving a seizure of up to 20 kg. or more; and for charas and hashish, small quantity is up to 100 gms. while the commercial quantity is 1 gram or more. Separate small and commercial thresholds have been prescribed for various drugs banned under NDPS Act. 

The Act takes a serious view of repeat offenders prescribing rigorous imprisonment of up to one-and-a-half times of the maximum term of imprisonment for that offence and also fine that shall extend to one-and-a-half times of maximum amount of fine. Repeat offenders are liable to even face death penalty if they are convicted again of a similar offence depending on the quantity of drugs seized. 

According to the 2019 Report prepared for the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment by the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre of the AIIMS, cannabis and opioids are the most commonly used substances in India after alcohol. The Report of the Magnitude of Substance Used in India says that the survey has found more than three crore individuals had used cannabis products in five years, while 2.6 crore said that they used the opioids which include opium and its variants like heroin, swag and brown sugar and the availability of pharmaceutical opioids. It added that estimated 85 lakh people inject the drug. The Report states that while several Government agencies are mandated to enforce strict drug control laws and regulations, लेकिन वास्तविकता यह है कि आज की हमारी युवा पीढ़ी ड्रग्स की गिरफ्त में आ गई है । 

SHRI MANISH TEWARI (ANANDPUR SAHIB): Sir, this Bill represents a pure question of law. यह कानून का बहुत ही खालिस सवाल है । What is the question of law that is found in para 5 of the Statement of Objects and Reasons of the Bill. Para 5 states: “The amendment does not create any new offence but contains a legislative declaration that reference of clause (viiia) always meant the corresponding renumbered provision in clause (viiib) and the amendment seeks to rectify this anomaly by making changes in section 27A of the said Act in order to carry out the legislative intent of the statute, which has always been to read clause (viiib) in section 27A, and already stood therein.” 

Sir, the question is, can a substantive sentencing provision in criminal law be given retrospective effect by a legislative declaration. That is the substantive question of law which unfortunately this Bill does not address.

My learned friend, Mr. Mahtab read out Article 20 (1) of the Constitution of India. May I, with your permission, hon. Chairperson, Sir, read out that provision in my own manner? Article 20(1) states that no person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of the law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence, nor be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence. It goes on to say that no personal shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once; no person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself. Now, why was this safeguard inserted by the framers of the Constitution into this document way back in 1950? It is because it primarily encapsulates two of the founding principles or the ground norms of law. The first ground norm is that every person is presumed innocent until substantively proven guilty. This is the first principle of the law. The second principle of the law is, and this goes back almost to 2,500 BC, and has held the field in the evolution of classical legal theory, now for over 2,500 years.

The second principle of the law is that “no person can be punished except in accordance with a sentencing provision which is in force when the offence is committed”. If this Bill, Chairperson Sir, is accepted in the form in which the Government has proposed it, this would mean that Article 20 of the Constitution of India will become redundant, and we are going to open the floodgates of misuse. 

Look at the implications of what we are saying. What we are saying is that, suppose, there is an offence committed today, or for that matter, let me extend the argument differently. If I am carrying out a lawful activity today, five years down the line, you can amend the law with retrospective effect, then you make that lawful activity illegal and send me to prison. Is this the kind of legislation which this House intends to pass because this then sets a very dangerous precedent? And it absolutely takes away the principle of stability which is intrinsic to criminal law that if at any point in time in the future, any law can be brought and can be given effect retrospectively, then no person in this country can ever be safe. It has implications on the confidence which people have in our supreme legislative institutions. 

Even though the legislative intent of the NDPS (Amendment) Act, 2014 was very clear, still, with great responsibility, I would like to state that the Bill which has been brought now cannot validate a wrong which got committed in 2014. Between 2014 and 2021, unfortunately, if someone has to be sentenced in accordance with Section 27a of the NDPS Act, the fact is that he cannot be sentenced. And this is the consistent principle which has been upheld by the courts of law.

Mr. Chairperson, Sir, with your permission, let me refer to a judgment of the hon. Supreme Court with regard to the NDPS Act itself. वर्ष 2001 में इसी संसद ने एनडीपीएस के कानून में संशोधन किया । संशोधन करके उन्होंने फर्क किया कि जो स्मॉल क्वांटिटी है, उसे 60 ग्राम से नीचे की मात्रा में रखा और जो कमर्शियल क्वांटिटी है, उसे 250 ग्राम से ज्यादा किया । अब एक व्यक्ति थे, उनका नाम जवाहर सिंह था । अब जवाहर सिंह के पास 65 ग्राम स्मैक पकड़ी गई और कानून के हिसाब से उसको सजा दे दी गई । उसके वकील ने उच्चतम न्यायालय में जाकर गुहार लगाई कि साहब यह बेनेफिशियल लेजिस्लेशन है, यह संशोधित किया गया है और इसका मेरे मुवक्किल को लाभ मिलना चाहिए ।. 

What did the Division Bench of Justice S. B. Sinha, one of the more erudite Judges of the hon. Supreme Court, and Dr. Mukandin Sharma, hold in that case? Let me read it out. Hon. Minister, possibly, this will make you reflect on the legislation which you have brought before this House. 

The judges said, “It is now beyond any doubt or dispute that the quantum of punishment to be inflicted on an accused upon recording a judgment of conviction would be as per the law which was prevailing at that relevant time. As on the date of the commission of the offence and on the date of conviction there was no distinction between small quantity and commercial quantity, question of infliction of a lesser sentence by reason of the provisions of the amendment Act, in our considered opinion, would not arise.” The court further says, “It is also a well settled principle of law that a substantive provision, unless specifically provided for or otherwise intended by the Parliament, should be held to have a prospective operation. One of the facets of the rule of law is also that all statutes should be presumed to have a prospective operation only.” And the court went ahead and dismissed that appeal. जो कानून इस संसद ने लोगों को राहत देने के लिए पारित किया था, उसको पिछली तारीख से, रेट्रोस्पेक्टिव्ली लागू करके भी फायदा नहीं दिया जा सकता । यह उच्चतम न्यायालय ने एनडीपीएस के केस में, जो वर्ष 2001 का ऑर्डिनेंस था, उस ऑर्डिनेंस के ऊपर अपना फैसला सुनाया है । अब मुझे यह बात समझ नहीं आती कि अगर उच्चतम न्यायालय का यह रुख है, तो उसमें आप यह संशोधन क्यों लेकर आए हैं?

This Amendment Act that you have brought which talks about imprisonment from ten years to life is a substantive sentencing provision. How will any court allow it to have retrospective effect? If you read Clause 27A, it is a substantive sentencing provision. 

Let me read it out for the benefit of this House. “Whosoever indulges in financing directly or indirectly any of the activities specified in Subclauses (i) to (v) of Clause 8A of Section 2, or harbours any person engaged in any of the aforementioned activities shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years which may extend to 20 years, and shall also be liable to a fine which shall not be less than Rs.1 lakh but which may extend to Rs.2 lakh”. This is a substantive sentencing provision.

आप 10 साल से लेकर उम्र कैद तक की बात कर रहे हैं । एक लेजिस्लेटिव डिक्लेरेशन से आपको कौन सी अदालत इजाजत दे देगी कि वर्ष 2014 में हमारा मतलब यह नहीं था, हमारा मतलब यह था । आपको कौन सी अदालत इसको लागू करने की अनुमति देगी? मैं समझ सकता हूं कि वित्त मंत्रालय में एक धारणा है । मैं भी बहुत समय तक इनकम टैक्स डिपार्टमेंट का सीनियर स्टैंडिंग काउंसेल रहा हूं । 

The opinion is that there is no equity to tax and tax legislations can be provided for retrospectively. However, even insofar as taxing statutes are concerned, court has very clearly said that you can collect taxes with retrospective effect but penal provisions, compensatory provisions, cannot be applied retrospectively. माननीय मंत्री जी, मैं आपको पढ़ कर सुनाना चाहता हूं ।

This is a 1987 judgment in JK Spinning and Weaving Mills Vs. Union of India case. The judgment has made it well settled that there cannot be any retrospectivity in respect of penalty and confiscation. The judgment exactly says: “It will be against all principles of jurisprudence to impose penalty on a person or to confiscate his goods for an act or omission which was lawful at a time when such an act was performed or omission made but subsequently made unlawful by virtue of a provision of law.” 

There are several judgments to the same effect following this leading judgment like Chief Commissioner of Excise, Ahmedabad versus Orient Fabrics where the Supreme Court said that the Additional Duties of Excise Act की जो पीनल प्रोविज़ंस हैं, वे रेट्रोस्पेक्टिवली लागू नहीं की जा सकती हैं । Chief Commissioner of Excise, Mumbai versus Lal Mining Engineering Works; यह वर्ष 2007 का फैसला है । और भी काफी फैसले हैं, जिनमें ईवन टैक्सेशन स्टैट्यूट में यह बात बिल्कुल साफ की गई है कि उसमें भी जो पीनल प्रोविज़ंस हैं, कॉम्पनसेट्री प्रोविज़ंस हैं, उनको आप रेट्रोस्पेक्टिवली लागू नहीं कर सकते हैं । 

सभापति जी, आपके माध्यम से मैं बहुत ही आदर और सत्कार के साथ मंत्री जी से अनुरोध करना चाहता हॅूं कि मुझे नहीं लगता ‍कि आपका कानून किसी अदालत में टिकेगा । यह बेहतर रहेगा कि आप इस कानून को संशोधित कीजिए और इस पर यह कहिए कि आप जो अमेंडमेंट ले कर आए हैं, वे उस तारीख से लागू होंगेl It will come into force from the date on which this law gets notified. 

Since Mr. Chairperson has rung the bell, I just have one or two more submissions to make. On a slightly broader point, सभापति महोदय, जब से अफ़गानिस्तान में तालिबान का राज आया है, अफ़गानिस्तान की अर्थव्यवस्था बिल्कुल चरमरा गई है । वहां पर जो नशीले पदार्थों की उपज है और उसकी जो तस्करी है, वह बहुत तेज़ी से बढ़ी है । उसका एक बहुत दूरगामी परिणाम भारत में पड़ने वाला है । मुंद्रा पोर्ट में जो इतना बड़ा नशीले पदार्थों का ज़खीरा पकड़ा गया, यह उसकी जीती जागती मिसाल है कि अफ़गानिस्तान में जो घटनाक्रम चल रहा है, उसका सीधा-सीधा असर हमारे ऊपर पड़ रहा है । उसके अलावा इस मुल्क में जो सिंथेटिक ड्रग्स की समस्या है which is what is really afflicting our youth. Synthetic drugs are being manufactured in legitimate pharmaceutical factories. That is something which the Government has been completely unable to come to grips with.

मैं आपसे यह आग्रह करना चाहता हॅूं कि कानून संशोधित करने की जगह आप अपनी एनफोर्समेंट को चुस्त-दुरुस्त कीजिए । एनफोर्समेंट को चुस्त-दुरुस्त कर के ये जो नशीले पदार्थ भारत में आ रहे हैं, अफ़ानिस्तान से, और पाकिस्तान से ड्रोन्स के माध्यम से भेजे जा रहे हैं, इसको रोकने की कोशिश कीजिए । धन्यवाद ।

DR. KALANIDHI VEERASWAMY (CHENNAI NORTH): Sir, thank you very much for giving me an opportunity to speak on the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021. 

I would like to quote a couplet from Tirukkural authored by Thiruvalluvar, a poet who has written about everything under the Sun. He said 2000 years ago, and I quote:

“Eendral mugatheyum innadhal enmatru

Sandror mugathu kali”

This means a mother normally absolves or protects her children from any kind of crimes which they are accused of. But when even she will not support their addictive behaviour or drunken behaviour, what can you expect of learned people? 

So, the importance of staying without addiction is being exemplified even 2000 years ago. So many people have spoken about this Bill. This Bill was brought in 1985 and subsequently amended several times. In 2014, the Act was amended and there was a change in clause number where the punishment was not commensurate with the clause number. That has been rectified through this amendment. 

Sir, as every other speaker before me, Shri Mahtab and Shri Manish Tewari, has said that when you bring a Bill and say that it will be having a retrospective effect – instead of saying that it will be effective from 2014 you say that it will be having retrospective effect from hundred years – I do not know how many people will fall under this law where they will be found culpable. It was mentioned earlier that it will open floodgates for the future, where any kind of an amendment can be made with retrospective effect. I think this should be avoided. 

Sir, we are talking about an Act where you will have to understand what narcotic substances are and what psychotropic substances are. Narcotic drugs are substances that cause stupor, muscular relaxation and reduction or elimination of sensitivity. This is basically something where it removes pain. Whereas, psychotropic substances are chemical substances that act on the mind, that is on the conscious or subconscious mental life of an individual. This is something where the crux of the issue lies. The youngsters nowadays are getting carried away with these things.

Under this Act, we have 238 drugs. Going through the list of 238 drugs, I would really ask the Government in the cases that have been filed, how many of these drugs have been found in possession or in abuse. Out of 238 drugs, the commonly talked about drugs are only ganja, tetrahydrocannabinol, cocaine, and a few other chemical compositions. I would request the Government to see whether these 238 drugs are actually being abused and whether this list can be shortened. I do not even know if the enforcement agencies will have knowledge about all these drugs in question.

Talking about the amendment which is being brought, it is sad to note that the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court has observed that passing Bills without adequate debate has caused a lot of confusion in the judiciary. When we are talking about Bills without adequate debate, what can we speak about the Ordinances? This is a Bill which could have been brought in during the Winter Session. This was brought in on 30th September, 2021. This could have waited for two months. What was the need to bring out an Ordinance? Was it for a particular case? 

Our learned Member from Dhule, Maharashtra, has accused saying that it is so rampant in Bollywood. If he believes that this drug abuse is there only in Bollywood, I will say that he is in a paradise. I do not know what paradise he is in! Today, drug abuse, especially ganja, tetrahydrocannabinol, and cannabis, has pervaded into schools, forget about colleges and other walks of life. Today, school children have access to these kinds of contraband, and it is the duty of the Government to ensure that the sale of these drugs should be curtailed. When they are talking so proudly, or they take such a glee in talking about Bollywood, they do not raise a single question. Neither the treasury benches nor the media raised a single question about the huge haul of drugs which was caught in one of the ports. Why is it that everybody is silent about that? What is the status of the drugs, amounting to several thousands of Kgs. that were caught? There was no mention or talk about that. I feel that it is a sad state of affairs that we are talking about addiction. Let us not assume that the Government has brought in this Bill for the welfare of the citizens of this country. The hon, Member, who is not here now, is a doctor and will say that cigarette and alcohol are the two biggest threats and the biggest problems in this country.

The earlier Member was talking about cannabis being sold on the roads. Today, cigarettes are being sold on the roads. Though you have an advisory, which says that this can cause cancer and this should not be sold to the school children, how much of this is being enforced? You find shops outside schools, colleges, everywhere and the sale of cigarettes is rampant everywhere. Being a doctor, I can say that smoking does not have absolutely any medicinal benefit at all, arguably, because there is only one topic, pre-eclampsia, where they say that smoking probably reduces BP in ladies who are suffering from pre-eclampsia. But smoking has one of the biggest health hazards which causes a lot of respiratory problems and also cancer. It causes cancer not only in the lungs but also, in several parts of the body like pancreas, urinary bladder, etc. But we do not talk about smoking and alcohol. One of the biggest psychotropic substances which causes most of the social evils -- be it familial, personal, health-wise -- is alcohol. In my State, I have seen families who are suffering due to alcohol because these men die at a young age leaving their families destitute. So, when we have these kinds of issues before us, why are we talking so much about these drugs? We are not even taking adequate action against those people who are selling or trafficking such drugs. We are only targeting the people who are found in the possession of such drugs and that too, a small quantity. 

We have a law which says that people who are having the possession of such drugs in small quantities, should be imprisoned for six months. I find this very strange because there are several countries where some of these drugs, especially cannabis, have been legalised. I am not saying that this Government should legalise cannabis. But to say that a person who is in a possession of a small quantity of a drug will be penalised and will be sentenced to six months of jail, I think, it is unacceptable. I feel that we should give them adequate protection. Even the Government probably should take steps to ensure that rehabilitation is provided to these people. If these people cannot afford such a rehabilitation, the Government can sponsor such a rehabilitation for them. I think, that is a way forward instead of trying to see how a person can be victimised and can be taken to task. The Government legally permits the sale of alcohol throughout the country. 

In this kind of a situation, I would like to request the Government to take adequate steps to ensure that Ordinances of this nature, are not promulgated. The Government should give an opportunity for a discussion and debate on the subject in the Parliament.

कैनाबिस को कैसे डिफाइन करेंगे? हमारे मंदिरों में, कैसे कहूं, सब साधू लोग …* हैं । क्या हमें पता है कि वे क्या…*हैं? वे …*हैं, …* हैं, पता नहीं क्या…* हैं । हमारे यहां होली में भांग पीते हैं । भांग इसमें आती है या नहीं, वह भी बताइए । कल को उनको भी लेकर जाएंगे और कहेंगे कि तुम लोग भांग पी रहे थे, होली मना रहे थे । इन सारी चीजों का सोशल इम्पैक्ट, जिसके बारे में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने कहा, वह भी देखना होगा । इसलिए आप यह जो कदम उठा रहे हैं, I am not criticising the intention of the Minister. But on legality, it is wrong to implement the penal provisions with retrospective effect because you cannot penalise a person with retrospective effect. इसलिए इसे वर्ष 2014 से लागू करने वाली जो बात है, उसे छोड़कर इसे प्रॉसपेक्टिव कीजिए, कोई दिक्कत नहीं होगी । धन्यवाद ।

श्री सुमेधानन्द सरस्वती (सीकर) : अभी माननीय अरविंद जी ने एक बात कही है कि सब साधु लोग …* हैं । यह सब साधुओं के लिए कहना गलत बात है । … (व्यवधान)

श्री अरविंद सावंत : मैं अपने शब्द वापस लेता हूं । सभी साधु नहीं …*   हैं । 

संसदीय कार्य मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री तथा संस्कृति मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री अर्जुन राम मेघवाल) : आप यह गलत कह रहे हैं । आप अपने शब्द वापस लीजिए । सभी साधु …* हैं, यह आप गलत कह रहे हैं । … (व्यवधान)

श्री अरविंद सावंत : मैं यह कहूं कि कोई नहीं पीता, क्या वह अच्छा लगेगा? मैं अपने शब्द वापस लेता हूं । … (व्यवधान)

डॉ. आलोक कुमार सुमन (गोपालगंज): सभापति महोदय, धन्यवाद । मैं आपका आभार व्यक्त करता हूं कि आपने मुझे द नारकोटिक ड्रग्स एण्ड साइकोट्रोपिक सब्स्टैंसस (अमेंडमेंट) बिल, 2021 पर अपनी बात रखने का मौका दिया । वर्तमान परिस्थितियों को ध्यान में रखकर यह महत्वपूर्ण विधेयक लाया गया है । यह विधेयक प्रिंसिपल एक्ट, जो कि द नारकोटिक ड्रग्स एण्ड साइकोट्रोपिक सब्स्टैंसस एक्ट, 1985 को अमेंड करेगा । वर्ष 1985 में इस एनडीपीएस एक्ट को इसलिए लाया गया था कि जो भी नारकोटिक्स ड्रग्स के कानून हैं, उनको मजबूत किया जाए तथा उपयोग के लिए सही दिशा दी जाए ।

महोदय, एनडीपीएस एक्ट‍ वर्ष 1985 में इसलिए भी लाया गया था, ताकि हम इंटरनेशनल कन्वेंशन ऑन नारकोटिक ड्रग्स एण्ड साइकोट्रोपिक सब्स्टैंसस के प्रोविजन्स को अपने देश में लागू कर सकें । एनडीपीएस एक्ट, 1985 को वर्ष 1988, वर्ष 2001 और वर्ष 2014 में अमेंड किया गया था कि ड्रग्स एण्ड साइकोट्रोपिक सब्स्टैंसस के दुरुपयोग को रोका जा सके । आज देश में ड्रग्स का दुरुपयोग काफी बढ़ता जा रहा है । यह न केवल शहर तक सीमित है, बल्कि गांव-गांव तक पहुंच चुका है । ग्रामीण इलाके के न केवल युवाओं को, बल्कि सबको चपेट में ले रहा है । गरीब से गरीब बच्चे इसके प्रभाव में आ रहे हैं, जिससे कि अपने देश को काफी नुकसान हो रहा है । इन सब परिस्थितियों में इस विधेयक का आना बहुत ही महत्वपूर्ण एवं लाभदायक है । 

महोदय, वर्ष 2014 के एनडीपीएस एक्ट के अमेंडमेंट से पहले इलिसिट ट्रैफिक को परिभाषित किया गया था, लेकिन वर्ष 2014 में इसेंशियल ड्रग्स के क्लॉज को इंसर्ट किया गया और साथ में यह भी आवश्यक हो गया कि ऑनरेबल हाई कोर्ट, त्रिपुरा ने हाल ही में Court on its own Motion Vs The Union of India केस में महत्वपूर्ण जजमेंट दिया, जिसके कारण लेजिस्लेटिव चेंज, सेक्शन 27 ए में एनोमली दूर करने के लिए आवश्यक हो गया और इसके लिए एनडीपीएस (अमेंडमेंट) ऑर्डिनेंस, 2021 को 30 सितंबर 2021 को लाया गया, ताकि एनोमली को दूर किया जा सके । 

महोदय, अगस्त 2021 तक अवेलेबल डाटा के अनुसार देश में लगभग 15.1 करोड़ लोग, जिनकी उम्र 18-75 के बीच है, एल्कोहल का सेवन करते हैं, जो कि 17.1 परसेंट है । इसी प्रकार कैनाबिस, जो कि मारिजुआना के नाम से प्रसिद्ध है, इसका सेवन 2.90 करोड़ लोग करते हैं, जो 3.31 प्रतिशत है । ओपियड्स, जिसको हम ओपियम कहते हैं, इसका उपयोग 1.86 करोड़ लोग करते हैं, जो 2.12 परसेंट हैं । इसी प्रकार से सीडेटिव्स है, जिसका उपयोग अपने देश में लगभग 1.05 करोड़ लोग करते हैं, जो कि 1.21 परसेंट है । इनहेलेंट्स, जिसका उपयोग 51. 25 लाख लोग करते हैं, जो कि 0.58 परसेंट है । कोकीन, जो कि प्रसिद्ध ड्रग है एवं महंगी भी है, इसका उपयोग अपने देश में लगभग 9.40 लाख लोग करते हैं, जिसका परसेंटेज 0.11 है । एम्फेटामाइंस -टाइप स्टिमुलेण्ट्स, जिसका उपयोग अपने देश में 15.47 लाख लोग करते हैं, जो कि 0.18 परसेंट है । 

महोदय, इसी प्रकार हेलुसिनोजिन्स का उपयोग लगभग 11.01 लाख लोग करते हैं, जो 0.13 परसेंट है । इन आंकड़ों को देखने से यही पता चलता है कि नारकोटिक्स ड्रग्स एवं साइकोट्रोपिक सब्स्टैंसस का गलत उपयोग के लिए कानून बनाना अति आवश्यक है । 

महोदय, इसमें मेरा कहना है कि ड्रग एडिक्शन की आदत शहर से लेकर गांव तक को प्रभावित कर रही है । अगर इसको नहीं रोका गया तो यह देश की बड़ी आबादी को चपेट में ले लेगी, जिसके कारण देश को मैनपावर के साथ-साथ आर्थिक क्षति भी होगी । इसलिए यह आवश्यक है कि नशा मुक्त भारत अभियान को सभी वल्नरेबल जिलों में चलाया जाए । लोगों एवं युवाओं को शिक्षित और जागरूक किया जाए । संविधान के अनुच्छेद 47 में कहा गया है कि शराब और दूसरे नशीले पदार्थ, जो लोगों के लिए हानिकारक हैं, इन पर रोक की दिशा में सरकारें काम करेंगी । हमारे माननीय मुख्य मंत्री श्री नीतीश कुमार जी ने एक अप्रैल, 2016 से बिहार में पूर्ण शराबबंदी एवं पूर्ण नशाबंदी लागू की है । इससे बिहार नशा मुक्त बिहार की तरफ सफलतापूर्वक आगे बढ़ रहा है । 

यह भी कहा जाता है कि इससे पांच हजार करोड़ रुपए राजस्व की हानि हो रही है, लेकिन यह डाटा है कि शराबबंदी से जनता के 10 हजार करोड़ रुपए बच रहे हैं, जिससे गरीब, निर्धन का जीवन बच रहा है और उनकी कमाई का पैसा उनके परिवार पर व्यय हो रहा है । हमारे आदरणीय मुख्यमंत्री, श्री नीतीश कुमार जी का यह कदम अभिनंदनीय है । 

महोदय, मैं यहां यह बताना चाहता हूं कि सरकार ने हेल्थ के क्षेत्र में Sustainable Development Goals के कई टारगेट को अचीव किया है, जो विश्व स्तर पर सराहनीय है । सरकार का यह भी प्रयास है कि Sustainable Development Goals के सभी टारगेट्स को समय से पहले पूरा किया जाए । अगर हम सभी टारगेट्स को समय से पूरा कर लेते हैं, तो निश्चित रूप से भारत विकसित देश की श्रेणी में खड़ा होगा । Sustainable Development Targets 3.5: Strengthen the prevention and treatment of substance abuse, including narcotic drugs and harmful use of alcohol से संबंधित है । वर्तमान विधेयक SDG को प्राप्त करने में सहायक होगा । डब्ल्यूएचओ के अनुसार भारत में 30 प्रतिशत लोग शराब पीते हैं, जिसमें 13 प्रतिशत लोग रोज शराब पीते हैं । खपत के मामले में भारत तीसरा सबसे बड़ा देश है । ग्रामीण भारतीय आमदनी का 45 प्रतिशत हिस्सा केवल शराब पर खर्च करते हैं । 20 प्रतिशत लोगों की मौत शराब पीकर गाड़ी चलाने से होती है । डब्ल्यूएचओ के वर्ष 2018 के आंकड़ों के अनुसार पूरे विश्व में 30 लाख लोगों की मृत्यु अल्कोहल से होती है तथा हर साल पांच लाख लोगों की मृत्यु नारकोटिक ड्रग्स के उपयोग से होती है, जिनमें से 30 प्रतिशत लोगों की मृत्यु ओवरडोज के कारण होती है । पिछले कुछ सालों में चार गुना देसी शराब, पांच गुना विदेशी शराब और 11 गुना बीयर की खपत देखने को मिली है ।

महोदय, युनाइटेड नेशंस के वर्ल्ड ड्रग रिपोर्ट के अनुसार 15 से 64 वर्ष उम्र वाले पांच प्रतिशत लोग विश्व में नारकोटिक्स एवं इलिसिट ड्रग्स के एडिक्टेड हैं । उनमें एडिक्शन इस तरह से बढ़ रही है कि आने वाले 10 सालों में यह बढ़ कर 30 प्रतिशत हो जाएगा । 

अगर मैं अपने देश की बात करूं तो वर्ष 2019 में भारतीय सिक्योरिटी एजेंसीज़ ने दो मीट्रिक टन से ज्यादा इलिसिट हिरोइन को जब्त किया है, जब कि वर्ष 2018 में 1.2 मीट्र‍िक टन जब्त किया गया । विगत, 1.89 लाख नारकोटिक्स केसेज रजिस्टर्ड किए गए हैं, जिनमें 2.31 लाख ड्रग स्मगलर्स अरेस्ट हुए, उनमें 1500 विदेशी स्मगलर्स शामिल थे । 

महोदय, नारकोटिक्स क्राइम रिकॉर्ड ब्यूरो के अनुसार 10 अगस्त, 2021 तक लगभग 910 लोगों को The Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1988 के अंतर्गत जेल भेजा गया है । वर्तमान विधेयक के पास होने से नशे में लत लोगों को नशे से मुक्ति मिलेगी और जो लोग गलत उपयोग करते हैं, उन पर रोक लगेगी । 

महोदय, मैं इसी के साथ इस बिल का समर्थन करते हुए अपनी बात समाप्त करता हूं ।

SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SADANAND SULE (BARAMATI): Thank you, Sir, for letting me speak on the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Bill, 2021. It is really an irony to stand here and have a long important debate on a subject like drugs and drug abuse. The issues related to drug are not just in India but they are also all over the world. It is one of the biggest challenges the youth in India and the world faces. I think, it is a very serious debate and we must put all our minds to it to resolve this issue rather than just throwing things at each other in this debate. The hon. Minister said that it is just to effect a small clerical change that she had brought this Bill. Since this issue is so large and, actually, it is a burning issue amongst the youth, it would have been nicer if the Government had come up with a broader Bill which would have, really, included topics of addressing this issue and not just doing something because the Court said it. Even more interesting is that in this Session we did not debate the Farm Laws Repeal at all but we are spending four hours on rectifying a small clerical mistake. It is really an irony that we are spending four hours on just a clerical change. Actually, it is quite disappointing, Sir. 

I would not repeat because most of the things have been said but I would just like to bring to the notice of the hon. Minister one thing. What she really said, which is a repeat of what Mr. Premachandran said when he was introducing the Bill that the State cannot make a law taking away the Fundamental Rights envisaged in Part-III of the Constitution it is a taking away, actually, from the part of Article 21 which talks about the Fundamental Rights.

So, I think, the hon. Minister really needs to explain this because this is something which has already been discussed. I want to support this Bill but I am not sure whether ‘retrospective’ is the solution to it. I think, what we really need to do is to find a way to stop this menace. What I am seeing is that the Government is resorting to knee-jerk solutions. It is always like this. कहीं कोई केस हो जाता है, उसका मीडिया-ट्रायल हो जाता है । उसके बाद सत्तापक्ष एक बात बोलता है, विपक्ष दूसरी बात बोलता है । यह ड्रग के मेनेस है, यह यूपीए वर्सेस एनडीए नहीं है । यह इस देश की बड़ी प्रॉब्लम है, हमारे बच्चों की बड़ी प्रॉब्लम है । I think, we need to take a larger view on this drug issue. It is not You versus Us. 

I was listening to Mr. Bhamre who is one of the finest MPs we have. He comes from the same State from where I come. I was actually a little disappointed with his speech. I was confused. It is because he is a very illustrious Doctor; he is an Oncologist. His speech was a little confusing for me to understand. It is unfortunate that he is not here. What drug should be there for use to treat cancer vis-à-vis what is eating into the youth of today, I think, that clarity did not come from his speech. What was really even sad and a little disappointing was to corner a certain institution. He talked about Bollywood. I see no reasons. Bollywood is too strong, and they do not need any of us to defend. But I would like to mention some of the points. My friend, Mr. Kalanidhi from DMK also defended the Bollywood. As regards the data, I want to take a little reference from my colleague, Mr. Gurumoorthy who is from YSRCP. He gave so much data about it. Now, I have one small question to Dr. Bhamre. When there is so much data PAN India, why is only Maharashtra’s Bollywood getting cornered? My question to this Government is this. Bollywood is really put into a corner as there are some evil people who only do drugs. I think, it is really very disappointing. It is not fair to put a fraternity in corner. Are you trying to tell me that no other fraternity has drug addicts? It is very unfortunate that you do a media trial to anybody in a particular fraternity, especially when the contribution of that unit has to be registered. 

Sir, it is an industry. It gives crores of jobs to the people. It also gives international visibility to India. India’s Bollywood stars give an identity to Indians all over the world. It is not just glamour. There is a lot of hard work, there is a lot of dedication, and there is a lot of commitment. This is the same Government which uses a lot of Bollywood stars to push in social messages. So, how does Bollywood become bad then? It is really sad that we are making one case or two cases without any proof. There are young girls being called once, twice, or thrice to the offices of NCB. Why are these young actresses or young actors being called all the time? What happened to all those cases? It happens once in three days, you see it in the media, and the story is gone. I would definitely refer to what Mr. Kalyan Banerjee said in his speech. He is talking about the Officers. This is a wonderful Bill you have brought. You are doing it with retrospective effect. But what happens to all these Officers who misuse and abuse their positions? 

There is a case of one of my colleagues in Maharashtra. His son-in-law was put in jail for nine months. उनके दामाद को नौ महीनों तक जेल में रखा । क्या कारण था? उनके पास गांजा नहीं था, वह तंबाकू निकला । I myself work against tobacco.

मेघवाल जी, इस देश में गुटखा बैन करने वाला राज्य कोई होगा, तो वह मेरा महाराष्ट्र है । श्री अजीत पवार जी जब उप-मुख्य मंत्री थे, तब उन्होंने गुटखा बैन किया था । ड्रग्स तो बहुत आगे की बात है, हम तो तंबाकू के खिलाफ, गुटखे के खिलाफ लड़ते हैं । इसके खिलाफ आपके साथ क्यों नहीं लड़ेंगे? हम ड्रग्स के खिलाफ आपके साथ कदम मिलाकर चलेंगे, लेकिन आप इन ऑफिसर्स का क्या करेंगे? मैं अभी तक यकीन नहीं कर पा रही हूं कि क्या किसी का दामाद होना कोई गलती है? उनके दामाद को नौ महीनों तक जेल में रखा गया । उनके छोटे-छोटे बच्चे अपनी मां से पूछते थे कि हमारे बाबा कहां गए? उनकी मां बच्चों से कहती थीं कि बाबा जेल में गए । किस कारण गए? तंबाकू के कारण गए? आपको पता होगा, there is a system when you arrest somebody under this Section. There is a kit; there are protocols to be followed. What happened to that kit? Are you trying to tell me that you do not know the difference between Gaanja and Tobacco? You arrest people like this, be it the young women working in Bollywood or the people holding political positions. What is going on in NCB? If there are false cases, who will give back the lives to that family? Is there no accountability of the Government? Be it ours or be it theirs, we are willing to work to end that menace but we will not tolerate injustice by any Officer against anybody by misusing his position. 

And, that is exactly, I think, what the essence of this Bill should be. You cannot use your position and abuse it. You cannot plant drugs, arrest people, take selfies with them, put them in social media and selectively leak information to the media. How does the media know everything before even people know about it? So, who are these officers and who is going to be accountable? यदि ड्रग्स के खिलाफ लड़ाई तो then, go after the big fish. छोटे बच्चों के पीछे पड़ने से कुछ नहीं होगा । 

Another thing is, addiction is an illness. None of these people, whom you are calling, are drug dealers. They are addicts. यदि उनके यहां मिला होगा, तो इसका मतलब उनको बीमारी है । First of all, we have no evidence also. I can tell you that there are so many cases about this. Today there is no time here to speak on that. But I would like to tell you that there are cases which have so many flaws. They do not even test the person who is arrested. 

So, how do you know that a person has consumed or has drugs? Or, even if they do not have drugs, they are kept in jail for 30 days. Is this the kind of law that we are living with? Just at the whims and fancies of one officer, they are kept in the jail. Is this the kind of power we are going to give to an officer who just misuses it and abuses it politically, socially and blackmail people? They will call and ask for lakhs and crores of rupees from people. This is not justice. This is not the justice that this Government talks about. So, I urge this Government to give justice. Take this Bill back. We are not against fighting. We will walk with this Government for a law to fight against this menace. But we definitely want them not to crucify people. 

Like this, there are 26 fake cases of blackmailing. You talk about Bollywood. We are so proud in this House that we have Hema Ji; we have Kirron Kher Ji and I think we have Mr. Sunny Deol whom I have not seen in a while. But Hema Ji and Kirron Ji are such good speakers and fine women. They are not just representing the Bollywood. They represent and I feel they are close to them because they are one of us; they are one of the most elegant ladies we have. We are so proud that they joined politics and they are a part of our Parliament today. So, it is really unfair to call Bollywood names, and it is something I think we should all put our minds to it and not corner any fraternity, especially Bollywood, which is so wonderful and contributing in all social causes of India.

The other last point is, prevention is much better than cure. So, why are we not looking at prevention and looking at the larger picture in this House when you bring Bills for legislation? They do not come here for correction. The largest supreme temple of democracy is our Indian Parliament. It is the largest democracy in the world. Then, are we going to spend hours on small corrections? Why do we not take the larger face of this and look at the whole larger picture? Have an extensive debate and bring in a comprehensive Bill. That is what we are asking for. It would have been much nicer.

I want to bring to your notice another small point which is beyond this Bill. It is about the fertilizers. This is something which came in my reading in the newspaper about 5-6 months ago. There is a fertilizer subsidy which the Government of India gives to the farmers. They are very proud of that. 

We are all proud about the subsidies which are given to our farmers. There is a cartel in a certain State. I would not name the State because that is not why of I am saying this. But the subsidy, which goes for rice and food, is moved towards marijuana. This is what is done because naturally if there is marijuana available, if it is planted somewhere, this subsidy goes there. So, there is a big story even in the media that all the subsides, which go for rice and food, are diverted towards marijuana. So, what are the interventions of this Government? What interventions are you doing to stop such subsidies? I think this is what the larger picture is. I think you need to take the larger picture and not just be stuck with the personalities. 

I would really like to bring it back to the notice of this House that we would definitely like to support a Bill which will help eradicate drug and psychotropic substances abuse. But I think any consumer needs emotional help. He does not need to go to jail. Jail does not resolve problems. It aggravates problems. So, if a child or a human being is an addict, he needs to go or she needs to go to a rehabilitation centre and not to a jail.

So, again, my humble request to the hon. 303-Government is this. You have a very good strength. You know, you have a lot of strength. It is not that we see it always. But I request them that they must bring a comprehensive Bill. We will, in one voice, send a message to this nation that India stands against drugs and we will not tolerate any such things.

So, if you want us to support this, please take this Bill back and bring a comprehensive Bill. Let us form a committee for this and get all the addictions out of this nation. Thank you, Sir.

श्री रतन लाल कटारिया (अम्बाला): सभापति महोदय, मैं सरकार द्वारा लाए गए नार्कोटिक ड्रग्स एंड साइकोट्रॉपिक सब्सटैंसेज (संशोधन) बिल-2021 का समर्थन करने के लिए खड़ा हुआ हूं । आज जिस प्रकार से नशे की लत सारी दुनिया को अपनी चपेट में ले रही है, उसका संज्ञान न केवल भारत, बल्कि दुनिया के सभी देशों ने मिलकर लिया है और संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ ने भी इसका संज्ञान लिया है । इसको लेकर इंटरनेशनल नार्कोटिक्स कंट्रोल बोर्ड की भी स्थापना की गई है । अलग-अलग प्रकार से सारी दुनिया की तीन कन्वेंशन्स इस नार्कोटिक्स के विषय को लेकर संपन्न हो चुकी हैं । इन कन्वेंशन्स में सारे विश्व ने मिलकर इस पृथ्वी से नशे को पूरी तरह से समाप्त करने के लिए संकल्प लिया है । इसके बावजूद यह कहीं न कहीं, किसी न किसी रूप में देखने को मिलता है । 

महोदय, भारतवर्ष में नशे की लत को रोकने के लिए तीन स्तरों पर कई विभाग मिलकर काम कर रहे हैं । मिनिस्ट्री ऑफ होम के अंतर्गत नार्कोटिक्स विभाग ड्रग्स के फैलाव को रोकने के लिए, इसकी तस्करी को रोकने के लिए सारे देश में काम करता है । इसके जगह-जगह पर रीजनल ऑफिसेज बने हुए हैं और इसके साथ ही साथ हमारे देश का स्वास्थ्य विभाग ऐसे लोगों का इलाज करता है, जो ड्रग्स का शिकार हुए हैं और जिनको ड्रग्स के कारण कई प्रकार की बीमारियां लग जाती हैं । ऐसे लोगों का इलाज करने के लिए भी स्वास्थ्य विभाग काम करता है । इसके साथ ही साथ मुझे सामाजिक अधिकारिता और सामाजिक न्याय विभाग में राज्य मंत्री के रूप में आदरणीय प्रधान मंत्री जी के नेतृत्व में काम करने का मौका मिल चुका है । उस समय सामाजिक अधिकारिता मंत्रालय में एक महत्वपूर्ण विंग बना, जो इस ड्रग एडिक्शन को लेकर काम करता है । पिछले साल 15 अगस्त को सारे देश के 272 जिलों में नशा मुक्ति अभियान चलाया गया और डिपार्टमेंट ने इस बात का प्रण लिया कि आने वाले समय में हम इस देश के 100 जिलों में नशा मुक्ति अभियान को लेकर काम करेंगे ।  हम सारे देश को नशे से छुटकारा दिलाएंगे । जैसा मैंने कहा कि संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ और विश्व के अन्य फोरम, जो इस विषय को लेकर बने हैं, उन्होंने समय-समय पर अपनी बातें इस दुनिया के सामने रखी हैं । आज एनडीपीएस बिल में अमेंडमेंट का जो यह विषय आया है, इसके अंतर्गत हम धारा 27 (A) के अंतर्गत एक मामूली से परिवर्तन की बात लेकर आए हैं । हालाँकि इसमें कोई नए विषय की एडिशन नहीं है । यह अमेंडमेंट केवल वर्ष 1985 का जो बेसिक एक्ट है, उस एक्ट के अंदर जो समय-समय पर परिवर्तन हुए और वर्ष 2014 में भी एक परिवर्तन हुआ, वह परिवर्तन करते समय उसमें एक छोटी सी चूक हो गई, एक बात छूट गई । उस छोटी सी चूक का सहारा लेकर त्रिपुरा हाई कोर्ट के अंदर जब एक केस गया, ड्रग एडिक्शन का एक मामला गया तो हाई कोर्ट ने वहाँ पर टिप्पणी की कि एक्ट के अंदर कहीं न कहीं थोड़ी कमी रह गई है, जिसके कारण हम इस केस के अंदर कोई पूरा निर्णय नहीं ले सकते । जो एक्ट की मूल भावना थी, उसके ऊपर कहीं न कहीं यह टिप्पणी आई और सजा होने से कुछ लोग बच गए । इसलिए दोबारा से फिर इस प्रकार की अमेंडमेंट आई है । 

पनिशमेंट के जो प्रावधान किए गए हैं, बड़े कड़े प्रावधान इस एक्ट के अंतर्गत किए गए हैं, उनको लागू करने के लिए ऐसा किया गया है । जैसा कि हम सब जानते हैं कि कहीं न कहीं दवाईयों के अंदर भी ड्रग्स का थोड़ा-बहुत, जो प्रेसक्राइब लिमिट है, उसके अंतर्गत जो हमारी फार्मास्यूटिकल कंपनीज हैं, जो दवाईयाँ बनाती हैं, उनके अंदर भी कहीं न कहीं इसका प्रयोग मनुष्य का जीवन बचाने के लिए किया जाता है । जो वे कुछ आइटम्स हैं, उन आइटम्स को छोड़कर बाकी जो नशे का व्यापार है, उसको सारे देश में बंद करने के लिए, उस पर अंकुश लगाने के लिए सरकार दिन-रात काम कर रही है । मैं हरियाणा का रहने वाला हूँ । मेरे लोक सभा क्षेत्र के साथ पंजाब की बहुत लंबी सीमा लगती है ।  पिछले वर्षों में पंजाब में जिस तरह से नशे के व्यापार ने हमारे नवयुवकों का जीवन बर्बाद किया है, वह एक सोचने वाला विषय है । हम किस प्रकार से अपने देश के नौजवानों को इस लत से बचा सकते हैं, इसके ऊपर मंथन करने की भी बहुत बड़ी आवश्यकता है । इसके साथ-साथ हम देखते हैं कि जो राष्ट्र नशे के पदार्थों की तस्करी करते हैं, उनके ऊपर भी भारत सरकार शिकंजा कस रही है । कई बार देखने को मिलता है कि हमारे देश के अंदर बॉर्डर से नशे की कई बड़ी-बड़ी खेपें दिखाई दीं, तो हमारी फोर्सेस ने उन सब को जब्त करने का बहुत बड़ा काम किया है ।

महोदय, कई बार हमारी चिंता इसलिए भी बढ़ जाती है कि हम पहले सुनते थे कि पाकिस्तान से ड्रग्स हमारे देश में काफी आती है और इसके साथ ही चाइना से भी आने की बातें हम सुनते रहते हैं, क्योंकि ये देश कहीं न कहीं भारत की उभरती हुई शक्ति को देखकर भयभीत हैं । वे कहीं न कहीं अपनी इस रणनीति के अंतर्गत काम कर रहे हैं कि भारत को किस प्रकार से क्षति पहुंचाई जाए? कोई क्रॉस बॉर्डर टेररिज्म का सहारा लेकर हमारे देश में दखल करने की कोशिश करता है । पिछले कुछ महीनों से अफगानिस्तान, जो हमारा मित्र देश है, भारत ने पिछले कई वर्षों से दिन-रात वहां की सरकार के साथ मिलकर काम किया है, वहां के विकास के लिए काम किया है । लेकिन जब से तालिबान ने वहां के प्रशासन पर कब्जा किया है, तब से भारत की आशंकाएँ और बढ़ी हैं कि एक और थर्ड प्लेयर हमारे देश के अंदर नशे के कारोबार को बढ़ावा देने के लिए कोई षड्यंत्र रच सकता है । लेकिन जैसा कि मैंने जिक्र किया कि हमारी सरकार होम डिपार्टमेंट के माध्यम से, स्वास्थ्य डिपार्टमेंट के माध्यम से, सोशल जस्टिस डिपार्टमेंट के माध्यम से, और इसके साथ ही आदरणीय निर्मला सीतारमण जी हमारे बीच हाउस में बैठी हैं, मैं इनका बहुत-बहुत आभार प्रकट करना चाहता हूं कि इन्होंने नशा मुक्ति के काम को सारे देश के अंदर बढ़ाने के लिए जिस प्रकार से कई सौ करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान बजट के अंदर किया है और उस बजट के बल पर हम 272 जिलों में नशा मुक्ति केन्द्र चला रहे हैं । आने वाले समय में अपने देश के सौ जिलों में से एक भी केस नशे का न मिले, उस दिशा में हम काम कर रहे हैं

माननीय सभापति: कटारिया जी, अब आप कनक्लूड कीजिए ।

श्री रतन लाल कटारिया: सर, जिस प्रकार से हमें सहायता मिली है, आज इस देश के कॉलेजों के माध्यम से, स्कूलों के माध्यम से, हमारे देश का जो स्पोर्ट्स डिपार्टमेंट है, उसके माध्यम से, एनसीसी के माध्यम से और एनजीओ के माध्यम से आज हमारे देश के अंदर सैंकड़ों ऐसी ऑर्गनाइज़ेशंस काम कर रही हैं, जो हमारे देश को, हमारे नौजवानों को नशे की लत से बचाने का काम कर रही हैं । आज जिस प्रकार से यह छोटा सा अमेंडमेंट सरकार ले कर आई है, इसमें कोई नई क्लॉज़ शामिल नहीं है । It is an anomaly, जो थोड़ी सी बची थी, उसको दूर करने का प्रयास हम इस बिल के माध्यम से कर रहे हैं । मैं इस बिल का समर्थन करते हुए अपने इस संकल्प को फिर से दोहराना चाहूंगा कि हम अपने देश से नशे की आदत को समाप्त करने के लिए सारे भारतवासी मिल कर काम करेंगे और जो भी देश बुरी नीयत से, हमारे देश के अंदर नशे की तस्करी करने की कोशिश करेगा तो भारत उसका मुंह तोड़ जवाब देगा और किसी भी कीमत पर उनको सज़ा से नहीं छोड़ा जाएगा । धन्यवाद ।

SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURESH (MAVELIKKARA): Sir, thank you very much for giving me an opportunity to put forth my views on the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Bill, 2021, which seeks to replace an Ordinance promulgated on 30th September this year.

The most important question concerning this Bill has been raised by several of my colleagues here that how can a criminal law be amended with retrospective effect. I am repeating the same question as the Government is committing an error in moving this Bill and the Government must redraft the Bill and come afresh.

I would also quote the Chief Justice of India who stated that the legislature has passed laws without conducting studies or assessing their impacts, and this half-baked legislation is a perfect example of the sentiment expressed by the Chief Justice of India. 

The Statement of Objects and Reasons of the Bill states and I quote, “The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Bill, 2021 would replace an Ordinance promulgated in September to correct a drafting error in the 2014 Amendment to the Act. Before the 2014 Amendment, Clause (viii-a) of Section 2 contained sub-clauses (i) to (v) which defined the term `illicit traffic’. This clause was re-lettered as clause (viii-b) by the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Amendment) Act, 2014, as a new clause (viii-a) in Section 2 defining `essential narcotic drugs’ and was inserted.” 

“… However, inadvertently consequential change was not carried out in Section 27A of the NDPS Act …”.

In a recent judgement, Justice Talapatra and Justice S. G. Chattopadhyay of hon. High Court of Tripura have held that until the appropriate legislative change occurs by amending Section 27A of the NDPS Act appropriately, sub-clauses (1) to (v) of clause (viii-a) of section 2 of the NDPS Act shall suffer the effect of deletion. So, an entire clause with such wide-ranging provisions of an important Act was ignored for seven long years, and now after the court pointed out that an effect of deletion will be resulted, the Government came running to the House.

Let us look at Section 27A of the NDPS Act. The provision reads that whoever indulges in financing, directly or indirectly, any of the activities specified in sub-clauses (i) to (v) of clause (viiia) of section 2 or harbours any person engaged in any of the aforementioned activities, shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term, which shall not be less than 10 years but which may extend to 20 years and shall also be liable to fine, which shall not be less than Rs. 1,00,000 but which may extend to Rs. 2,00,000 provided that the court may, for reasons to be recorded in the judgement, impose a fine exceeding Rs. 2,00,000. 

Now, we will look into the reason of Section 27A getting inoperable. The text of the provision says that offences mentioned under section 2 (viiia) sub-clauses (i) to (v) are punishable through Section 27A. However, section 2 (viiia) sub-clauses (i) to (v), which is supposed to be the catalogue of offences does not exist after the 2014 Amendment. So, when the catalogue or description of offence itself is absent, how could the main provision operate with efficiency and how will it dispense fullest justice? So, if Section 27A penalises a blank list or a non-existent provision, it can be argued that it is virtually inoperable. The High Court ruling further ordered that both the Central Government and the State Government shall publish a notification bringing about the content of this order, in short, for the public notice so that the requirement of Article 20 of the Constitution of India is not diminished. Article 20 of the Constitution guarantees protection against double jeopardy. Article 20 (1) says : “No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of the law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence, nor be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence”. 

I am not going into all the details because hon. Members have already mentioned it here, and many more Members are desirous of speaking on this Bill. One must note that the 16th Lok Sabha held its Sessions between June, 2014 and February, 2019 and during these five years 133 Bills were passed and 45 Ordinances were promulgated and not even once did the Government think of promulgating this Amendment till the Tripura High Court made a mention and pushed this incompetent Government towards reality. Therefore, even when the Bill is necessary in correcting a drafting error that makes an important clause inoperable, I would say that this Government is inefficient, incompetent, and lethargic in matters of governance. Its failure and wilful dithering on an important legislation in a subject related to narcotics Act is a serious lapse. 

With these words, I conclude my speech. Thank you, Sir.
